hook.en: When we compare what we observe with what we expect, we square the differences and add them up. The distribution of such a sum of squares is the chi-square distribution, the basis of many tests in the next chapter.
hook.kn: ಗಮನಿಸಿದುದನ್ನು ನಿರೀಕ್ಷಿಸಿದುದರೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸುವಾಗ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸಗಳನ್ನು ವರ್ಗಗೊಳಿಸಿ ಕೂಡಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ. ಅಂತಹ ವರ್ಗಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತದ ವಿತರಣೆಯೇ ಕೈ-ವರ್ಗ ವಿತರಣೆ; ಮುಂದಿನ ಅಧ್ಯಾಯದ ಅನೇಕ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗಳ ಆಧಾರ.

objectives.en: Define the chi-square variate and degrees of freedom
State its properties: mean n, variance 2n, mode n − 2

narration.en: When we compare what we observe with what we expect, we square the differences and add them up. The distribution of such a sum of squares is the chi-square distribution, the basis of many tests in the next chapter.
narration.kn: ಗಮನಿಸಿದುದನ್ನು ನಿರೀಕ್ಷಿಸಿದುದರೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸುವಾಗ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸಗಳನ್ನು ವರ್ಗಗೊಳಿಸಿ ಕೂಡಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ. ಅಂತಹ ವರ್ಗಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತದ ವಿತರಣೆಯೇ ಕೈ-ವರ್ಗ ವಿತರಣೆ; ಮುಂದಿನ ಅಧ್ಯಾಯದ ಅನೇಕ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗಳ ಆಧಾರ.

body.en: If $Z_1, Z_2, \dots, Z_n$ are independent $N(0, 1)$ variates, then $\chi^2 = Z_1^2 + Z_2^2 + \dots + Z_n^2$ follows the chi-square distribution with $n$ degrees of freedom (d.f.). The d.f. is the number of independent squares in the sum. In sampling, $\dfrac{\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2}{\sigma^2} \sim \chi^2_{n-1}$: one d.f. is lost because $\bar{x}$ is estimated.
body.kn: n ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ N(0, 1) ಚರಗಳ ವರ್ಗಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ n ಸ್ವಾತಂತ್ರ್ಯ ಮಟ್ಟಗಳ (d.f.) ಕೈ-ವರ್ಗ ಚರ. ಮಾದರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ Σ(x − x̄)²/σ² ಗೆ n − 1 ಸ್ವಾತಂತ್ರ್ಯ ಮಟ್ಟಗಳು.

narration.en: Square n independent standard normal variates and add them. The total follows the chi-square distribution with n degrees of freedom, the number of independent squares in the sum.
narration.kn: n ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ N(0, 1) ಚರಗಳ ವರ್ಗಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ n ಸ್ವಾತಂತ್ರ್ಯ ಮಟ್ಟಗಳ (d.f.) ಕೈ-ವರ್ಗ ಚರ. ಮಾದರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ Σ(x − x̄)²/σ² ಗೆ n − 1 ಸ್ವಾತಂತ್ರ್ಯ ಮಟ್ಟಗಳು.

narration.en: The teacher builds chi-square from squared normal variates and draws the curves for 2, 4 and 8 degrees of freedom.

say.en: Start with standard normal variates. Squaring removes the sign, so chi-square can never be negative.
Here are the curves for 2, 4 and 8 degrees of freedom. With more d.f. the peak moves right and the curve spreads.
The mean is n and the variance is 2 n. The peak, the mode, is at n minus 2.
Independent chi-squares add, and so do their degrees of freedom.

narration.en: Each value is χ² = Z₁² + … + Zₙ², the sum of n squared standard normal variates. Collect hundreds of them: the histogram follows the χ² curve with n degrees of freedom. It is never negative, skewed to the right, with mean n and variance 2n, and becomes more symmetric as n grows.

caption.en: Each value is χ² = Z₁² + … + Zₙ², the sum of n squared standard normal variates. Collect hundreds of them: the histogram follows the χ² curve with n degrees of freedom. It is never negative, skewed to the right, with mean n and variance 2n, and becomes more symmetric as n grows.
caption.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಬೆಲೆ χ² = Z₁² + … + Zₙ², n ಪ್ರಮಾಣಿತ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಚರಗಳ ವರ್ಗಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ. ನೂರಾರು ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಿ: ಆಯತ ಚಿತ್ರ n ಸ್ವಾತಂತ್ರ್ಯ ಮಟ್ಟದ χ² ವಕ್ರವನ್ನು ಅನುಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಅದು ಎಂದಿಗೂ ಋಣವಲ್ಲ, ಬಲಕ್ಕೆ ಓರೆ, ಸರಾಸರಿ n, ಚದುರಿಕೆ 2n.

tryThis.en: With 1 d.f., where do most values fall? Why?
Compare the observed mean and variance with n and 2n.
Increase the d.f. to 10. Is the curve still as skewed?

body.en: The $\chi^2$ curve lies between 0 and $\infty$ and is positively skewed; skewness falls as $n$ grows and for large $n$ it is nearly normal. Mean $= n$, variance $= 2n$, mode $= n - 2$ ($n > 2$). Additive property: the sum of independent $\chi^2$ variates is $\chi^2$ with d.f. added. Applications: testing a population variance, goodness of fit, and independence of attributes.
body.kn: χ² ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆ 0 ಯಿಂದ ∞ ವರೆಗೆ, ಧನಾತ್ಮಕ ವಿಷಮತೆ. ಸರಾಸರಿ n, ಪ್ರಸರಣ 2n, ಬಹುಲಕ n − 2. ಸಂಕಲನ ಗುಣ. ಉಪಯೋಗ: ಪ್ರಸರಣದ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ, ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆಯ ಉತ್ತಮಿಕೆ, ಗುಣಗಳ ಸ್ವಾತಂತ್ರ್ಯ.

points.en: Positively skewed; near normal for large n

narration.en: Increase the degrees of freedom. The curve moves to the right, spreads out and becomes more symmetric, getting closer to a normal curve.

tryThis.en: Set n = 2: the curve starts at its highest point.
Set n = 10. Is the peak at 8?
At n = 20, does the curve look nearly symmetric?

body.en: For χ² with n d.f., think "n, 2n, n − 2": the mean is n, the variance doubles it, and the mode is two steps back.
